title: Quasi-compact reduction for a proper-support complex
statement: Let S be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], let f:X\to S be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let E be bounded with coherent cohomology on X [def-pc-derived-category], with every cohomology sheaf supported on a closed subset proper over S [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. Then there is a quasi-compact open immersion j:X'\hookrightarrow X containing the union of the supports of all cohomology sheaves of E such that f':=f\circ j:X'\to S is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and the canonical map Rf_*E\to Rf_*Rj_*j^*E\cong Rf'_*j^*E [def-pc-derived-direct-image] (Rf_* of the adjunction map E\to Rj_*j^*E, followed by the composition isomorphism Rf_*\circ Rj_*\cong Rf'_*) is an isomorphism; in particular Rf'_*j^*E\cong Rf_*E.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Tag 08EV; label perfect-lemma-perfect-direct-image, proof: sentences beginning 'Let T be the union...' through 'Thus we may replace X by X''

proof.text: Because E is bounded, only finitely many cohomology sheaves are nonzero. The union T of their closed supports is proper over S by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-union-preimage](1), applied to the locally finite-type morphism f and the given proper supports.

source.place: Tag 08EV, proof of lemma-perfect-direct-image, paragraph beginning 'Let T be the union'

proof.text: Regard T with its reduced induced closed subscheme structure and use its closed immersion into X. By [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base](1) the morphism T\to S is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], in particular quasi-compact, and S is quasi-compact because it is Noetherian; hence T is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2); [lemma-nagata-immersion-shrink-to-closed-exists] therefore supplies a quasi-compact open immersion j:X'\hookrightarrow X containing T. The scheme X is locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft], because S is Noetherian (hence locally Noetherian) and f is locally of finite type. Local Noetherianity passes to the open subscheme X' by restriction of affine neighborhoods, so X' is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. The Noetherian scheme S is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Thus f'=f\circ j is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1): X' is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and S is quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 08EV, support reduction through 'there exists a quasi-compact open X'

proof.text: All cohomology sheaves of E are supported on T\subseteq X', so the supported-open pushforward statement [lem-pc-supported-open-pushforward] gives a canonical isomorphism E\cong Rj_*j^*E. Applying the general composition isomorphism [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image-composition] to j followed by f' identifies Rf_*E with Rf'_*j^*E. Thus the canonical map Rf_*E\to Rf_*Rj_*j^*E\cong Rf'_*j^*E, which is Rf_* of that isomorphism followed by the composition isomorphism, is an isomorphism.
